issues.description: The problem statement's UML and attribute list specify numberOfLecturers as type int, but the solution implementation declares the field as byte. This mismatched attribute type can confuse students about the intended type and lead to signature mismatches for related methods (constructor/setter) or failing tests that expect int.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the numberOfLecturers attribute type consistent with the UML/problem statement. Change the field declaration in the solution to int (private int numberOfLecturers) so it matches the specification and avoids confusion. Alternatively, if byte was intentional, update the problem statement UML and description to indicate byte explicitly.

issues.description: The solution's constructor declares its numberOfLecturers parameter as byte, whereas the problem/UML specify an int for that attribute. This constructor parameter type mismatch will confuse students implementing the constructor following the UML and may cause incompatibilities with expected tests/signatures.
issues.suggested_fix: Adjust the constructor parameter type to int to follow the UML and problem description (public Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors)). If byte is preferred, update the problem statement to indicate byte and ensure all related method signatures use byte consistently.

issues.description: The solution's setter for numberOfLecturers accepts a byte parameter (setNumberOfLecturers(byte ...)) while the problem statement and UML imply an int-typed attribute and setters/getters should use int. This method parameter mismatch may confuse students implementing/setters and lead to inconsistent API (getter returns int but setter takes byte in the solution).
issues.suggested_fix: Change the setter signature to accept an int (public void setNumberOfLecturers(int numberOfLecturers)) so it matches the UML and typical expectations. Also ensure getter/setter/field types are consistent (all int) across the implementation and documentation.
